I am an engineering and research master's student working at the intersection
of generative modeling, latent world models, reinforcement learning, and
numerical methods. I am completing CentraleSupélec's Engineering Degree in
Mathematics and Data Science alongside the M2 Mathematics and Artificial
Intelligence at Université Paris-Saclay.

Alongside my studies, I work as a Generative AI Engineer at MBDA on multi-agent
systems built around large language models. I previously worked as a Data
Scientist at TotalEnergies' Digital Factory. This site covers only public
research and deliberately excludes non-public professional work.

## How I approach research

I am drawn to hypotheses that sound compelling but can fail in informative
ways. My preferred workflow is to turn the hypothesis into a controlled
protocol, compare against strong baselines, examine numerical and statistical
failure modes, and keep the negative result when the evidence does not support
the original story.

That approach connects the public projects here: testing regularity as a
surrogate for few-step ODE error, separating latent-state decodability from
planning utility, and comparing learned compute allocation with simple
stopping diagnostics. The common aim is not a broader claim than the evidence
allows, but an experiment that another reader can inspect and challenge.

## Research interests

- generative models, diffusion, and flow matching;
- world models and latent representations;
- reinforcement learning, planning, and control;
- scientific machine learning and numerical methods;
- compute allocation and rigorous evaluation under finite budgets.

I am especially interested in what makes generative and world models reliable
when inference and evaluation budgets are finite, including their eventual use
for physical dynamics. This is a research direction of interest rather than a
claim about completed work.
